READ instead: (i) ICRP's own publication page (icrp.org, via alphaXiv) -- abstract says P23 'is supplemented and amended by ICRP Publication 89'; (ii) Wikipedia 'Standard person' (via alphaXiv) quoting ICRP 23 p.335's definition verbatim and stating ICRP 23 has no elemental data for a Reference Woman; (iii) Emsley's column as RESTATED in Wikipedia 'Composition of the human body' (Mass (kg) column cites Emsley 2011 p.83), fetched 2026-09-26, saved at d67/wiki_composition_human_body.txt; (iv) ICRP 110 (2009) standard tissues via Kanematsu arXiv:1508.00226 Table I. published_statement: ICRP 23 (as quoted by Wikipedia 'Standard person', p.335): 'Reference man is defined as being between 20-30 years of age, weighing 70 kg, is 170 cm in height, and lives in a climate with an average temperature of from 10 C to 20 C. He is a Caucasian and is a Western European or North American in habitat and custom.' ICRP abstract: 'A unique comprehensive work on the reference male and female, including data on mass of the various organs of the body, chemical composition of the body ... While still the major source of reference data, this report is supplemented and amended by ICRP Publication 89.' Emsley (as restated): the average 70 kg adult body contains N 1.8 kg, Ca 1.0, P 0.78, K 0.14, S 0.14, Na 0.10, Cl 0.095, Mg 0.019, Fe 0.0042, F 0.0026, Zn 0.0023, ... Li 0.000007 kg (7 mg) ..., with 'at least detectable traces of 60 chemical elements'; the page adds 'The numbers in the table are averages of different numbers reported by different references.' ICRP 23's own gram table: NOT READ here.
published_hypotheses: Reference Man is a single defined individual: male, 20-30 years, 70 kg, 170 cm, Caucasian, Western European / North American habitat (ICRP 23 p.335, READ via restatement)
ICRP 23 carries no elemental data for a Reference Woman (restatement)
ICRP 23 is supplemented and amended by ICRP 89 (2002) (ICRP page, READ); the revised reference male is heavier by 3 kg (restatement)

Emsley's figures are for 'the average 70 kg adult' and are compilations (the restating table: 'averages of different numbers reported by different references'); relative amounts 'vary by individual, mainly due to differences in the proportion of fat, muscle and bone'
a composition of 60 detected elements (restatement), of which the tree carries 59

rederivation.outcome: 13 of 13 checks pass (output in rederive/icrp-23-reference-man.out). The tree's arithmetic reproduces exactly: stock.HUMAN = 59-row fractions to 6 dp; listed sum 0.9999231; N 0.025683, P 0.011129; K 139.86 g ~ 140 g; superseded 0.0040 = 280 g; photosphere binds P at 1910.9 with Li at 91.757 %; CI binds P at 10.70, N 8.076. Sensitivity (bisection with renormalisation): Li flip at 7.629 mg (+8.98 %); P flip to Li below 715.7 g (-8.24 %); P flip to N at CI below 588.7 g (-24.5 %). Alternative data READ here move the binder at both destinations: ICRP 110 bulk -> photosphere Li 1752 (P 1395), CI C 9.02 (P 7.81); restatement P 350-490 g -> photosphere Li ~1761, CI N ~8.1; restatement Li 2.17 mg -> P binds with K second at 651.8. Caveat on ICRP 110: Kanematsu's regional elemental weights are density-and-mass-weighted means, and the population is 50 % male / 50 % female, so it prices a different reference body, not a corrected Reference Man.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested on this result. What ICRP 23 lacked in 1975: in vivo whole-body data for women and non-Western populations (ICRP 23 carries no Reference Woman elemental data; in vivo Reference Woman estimates came in 1990, per restatement), and the later anatomical review that became ICRP 89 (2002) and the voxel-phantom tissue set ICRP 110 (2009). Does having it change the conclusion? The source's own statement is not shown wrong: nothing here contradicts '780 g P in a 70 kg Reference Man' as a 1975 compilation for that defined male, and ICRP 23 itself could not be read. But the TREE's conclusion (D25: 'a reference adult binds on P at 10.70 against CI chondrite ... on P at 1911 against a stellar photosphere') does move with the later data: on ICRP 110's whole-body bulk (M/F mean, computed from READ Table I) the photosphere binder is Li (1752) and the CI binder is C (9.02). Evidence the other way: the magnitudes move by at most 1.2x (1911 -> 1752; 10.70 -> 9.02), so every order-of-magnitude conclusion (bulk-chemistry constraint, asteroid-class node near 10 kg/kg, star ~2e3 kg/kg) survives; and part of the move is a change of reference population (50/50 M/F, more adipose tissue), which is a hypothesis choice, not a correction of ICRP 23. So: the older data were incomplete for the class the tree uses ('adult'), and the binder identity -- not the scale -- depends on which data are taken.
grade_evidence: (1) The tree's use reproduces to the digit (13/13; P 1910.9, Li 91.757 %, P 10.70 vs N 8.076, K 140 g). (2) The binding-element identity sits within 8-9 % of two data: Li flips it at +8.98 % (7.629 mg), P at -8.24 % (715.7 g), both computed. (3) Those data have moved or are contested in sources READ here: ICRP says P23 is amended by P89; ICRP 110 via arXiv:1508.00226 gives P 0.813 %, which hands the photosphere to Li (1752 > 1395) and, with C 31.6 %, hands CI to C (9.02 > 7.81); the Emsley restatement's own fraction column gives P 0.5-0.7 % and Li 2.17 mg. (4) The tree drops the source's hypotheses 'male' and 'supplemented and amended by ICRP 89'. (5) Not WRONG: no refuting counterexample to ICRP 23 is shown -- its table was unreadable here, the V/Ga/O/C disagreements are discrepancies against a tertiary restatement and move nothing, and the ICRP 110 comparison changes the reference population. (6) Not STANDS: a moved datum moves the binder. Magnitudes (1.9e3, ~10 kg/kg) are robust to within 1.2x on every alternative tried.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading ICRP 23's whole-body table (Snyder et al. 1975) and ICRP 89's reference-male elemental values at source: if ICRP 89 male keeps P >= 715.7 g per 70 kg-equivalent (>= 1.021 % by mass) and a primary Li body-content measurement lies below 7.63 mg with its uncertainty, the photosphere binder P would be robust for the reference male and the grade would go to NARROWED (holds for Reference Man, not for 'an adult'). If the ICRP 89 male P fraction falls below 1.021 %, or a primary Li figure exceeds 7.63 mg, the tree's D25 binder statement at the photosphere would be contradicted for its own payload (still recorded, not repaired). A read of Emsley p.83 itself would settle the V, Ga, O and C discrepancies.
